groups.defect: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys like [z.string().toString()]. These create literal property names instead of a catchall or record, so the schema does not validate token responses as intended. Fix: use .catchall(), .passthrough() or z.record().

answer.reasoning:
All three suggestions point at the same lines (5-11/12) of minimumTokenResponseSchema. They report the same root defect: the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` produce literal property names rather than dynamic-field validation. They also propose the same fix (catchall, passthrough or record). Grouping them is clear.

They describe the consequence differently. s_95664fc2 and s_0034d203 say valid tokens fail validation. s_ffe6d591 says expiry fields get stripped. In practice both computed keys stringify to the same literal, so the second definition (z.unknown().optional()) overrides the first, and the result is the stripping behavior. Still, these are two descriptions of the effect of one defect, not separate defects. One edit at one place resolves all of them, so I set needsUnifiedComment to false.

That last choice is the only judgment call here, and it is exactly where the two judges disagreed. That is why decisive is false.
